analysis: The only changed file is a Swift test file, EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift. The changes visible in the patch are around lines 713-755 and sit in the base units at 692-726. In the pagedPoolLocksStepWithSchedulerConfig test, the comment is reworded. The stripe assertion changes from soloPrefillStripeTokens equal to defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens to prefillChunkSize equal to widePrefillChunkTokens, soloPrefillStripeTokens nil, and pool maxPrefillChunk equal to defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens. The patch also adds a new test, widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry, whose body is truncated in the excerpt. These changes touch no production code, auth, crypto, key handling, cache-at-rest behavior or network surface. The tests continue to pin the hermetic environment (the crash-guard path is /dev/null and the KV quantization policy is native). The prefix-cache tests (T-041) use ephemeral keys and isolated temp roots, and are unchanged in behavior. A test file has no runtime effect on the shipped provider. The production change that introduces widePrefillChunkTokens is not in the supplied batch. Its security-relevant aspects are pool sizing against the PagedSequenceKV precondition that a windowed update never exceeds maxPrefillChunk, which is an availability concern (a process abort rather than a throw) in EngineV2Factory. The integration pass should check that the production factory and these assertions agree. I cannot verify that here, and no finding is raised. The tail of the new test is truncated in the excerpt, so it was not fully examined.
